Security Clearance Type: None/Not Required Security Clearance Status: Not Required Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX. What You Will Do Collins Aerospace is seeking motivated Software Engineers join the Integrated Applications Engineering team supporting development of the Collins Flight Deck. This role offers the opportunity to work on real avionics programs and gain hands-on experience across the software lifecycle—from requirements and architecture through integration, verification, and delivery. This position will provide you the opportunity to work with Flight Deck software in an agile team environment. The team has an array of technical tasks available meant to develop engineers for the future. As part of the team, you will work alongside experienced engineers to help develop the software based on high-level system behaviors, decompose requirements, support avionics architecture development, and contribute to software verification activities. This is a strong fit for those who enjoy solving technical problems, learning complex systems, and collaborating across software, systems, and test disciplines. Immerse yourself in a full-time, Monday-Friday co-op session, that will run May/June- December (including the Fall semester; it is expected students will take a semester off from coursework to fully engage with this working mentorship opportunity). Collaborate with a cross-functional team of software engineers, integration specialists, and test engineers to design, develop, and deliver robust avionics software solutions. Support the development, analysis, and refinement of software requirements and interfaces to ensure alignment with system-level objectives. Contribute to the planning and development of software verification and testing strategies to ensure implementations meet functional and performance requirements. Participate in technical reviews of software requirements, design documents, and test procedures, incorporating feedback to improve the quality and effectiveness of your deliverables. Assist with software integration, debugging, and issue resolution in development, simulation, and testing environments. Clearly communicate technical progress, challenges, and potential solutions to team members, mentors, and stakeholders to ensure alignment and successful project outcomes What You Will Learn How avionics systems are developed across the full engineering lifecycle, from concept and requirements through integration and verification. How to work with software requirements, architecture artifacts, and verification methods used on real aerospace programs. How to collaborate effectively in a multidisciplinary engineering environment with mentorship from a dedicated technical “copilot” and other experienced team members. How to apply structured problem solving, technical communication, and engineering rigor in a safety-critical domain. Qualifications We Prefer Must be pursuing Bachelor's or Advanced degree in Aerospace Engineering, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, or a related STEM discipline. and actively enrolled through the completion of the internship/co-op session. Must have a minimum of 60 hours of credit by the start of the internship / co-op session. Experience in C/C++ and Python Experience may be obtained through on-the-job experience, research, coursework, or projects. Qualifications We Prefer Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment. Prior RTX internship, co-op, or work experience. From volatile markets to climate shifts, independent operators face mounting pressure. While sustainable investments often yield the best long-term returns, they require financial clarity and capital that fragmented legacy systems can't provide. By the end of your internship you'll… - Collaborate with the team as the owner for a full-stack feature built into our core product. As the engineering owner, you'll break down your project into granular pieces and practice good project management hygiene, triaging and prioritizing new issues that come in. - Collaborate with our Product team to influence prioritization of feature ideas and requests with insights from our audience. - Embed yourself deeply in understanding the state of farm finance, building a strong intuition about customer needs and audience segmentation. Comfortable taking on ambiguous problems and creating elegant technical solutions - Exhibits strong computer science fundamentals and an eagerness to learn - Bonus: Experience with Typescript, React, React Native, and/or Next.js. - Bonus: Track record of building and shipping complex software projects - Bonus: Experience in agriculture Our tech stack - Next.js / React application written in Typescript - Hosted on Google Cloud - Firestore & Google Cloud Storage & Postgres for data storage - BigQuery & Data Studio for data insights What makes this internship special - Make a real difference: Build features that help farmers adopt sustainable practices and grow their businesses - Experience life at a high growth startup: see the complete product development cycle, from design to deployment in a fast-paced environment - Get personalized mentorship: Work directly with senior engineers who are invested in your growth - Join a mission-driven team: Experience startup culture while helping build the future of sustainable agriculture - Work closely with customers: Your work will help real farms and agribusinesses across America succeed - and you'll get to meet some of them Values - Real Talk – We create space for ourselves and others to be straightforward, vulnerable, and accountable. - Reach Understanding – We are driven by curiosity and empathy to learn about our customers, team, and world. - title: Software Engineering Intern
qualification_text: Software Engineering Intern [Spring/Summer 2027] New York City Melius — New York City Engineers have Cursor. Lawyers have Harvey. The office of the CFO has Ramp. Every knowledge profession has been handed a platform that lets them orchestrate agents and scale their output by an order of magnitude — except the people who actually make the things we look at, watch, and listen to. Melius is the agents lab for creative work. We build agentic interfaces to all the work that goes into building the next generation of images, video, audio and so much more. Generative media canvas, timeline editor, asset manager, and much more, built native for agents. Using Melius, users can spend more time being creative and let go of the century old legacy tools that only acted as constraints to their imagination. We're backed by General Catalyst, Vine Ventures, Genius Ventures, and Antifund, and built by a team of second-time founders, former engineering leaders from Ramp, and operators who came up through top-tier VC and PE. We move fast, ship every day, and have strong opinions about craft. THE ROLE This is not a “summer project” internship. Expect to be treated exactly as a full time engineer would be from the first day at your job. There will be dozens of projects that you lead and are expected to educate both customers and other members of the team on. The stack: Next.js and a real-time CRDT canvas on the frontend, NestJS / MikroORM / Postgres / Temporal / Turbopuffer on the backend, and the agent and model orchestration layer that ties it all together. High level activities for the internship might include: - Building new tools for our agent end-to-end — what it can do on the canvas, what it can change in the timeline editor, and how it can semantically search in the asset manager. - Sitting in on user sessions, watching a creative hit a rough edge, and shipping the fix that same hour. - Adding evals and traces that tell us, honestly, whether the agent got better this week. - Polishing canvas interactions that thousands of creatives touch every day — the small details users never explicitly notice but always feel. You'll work directly with senior engineers and the founders. Expect fast feedback, real code review, and more ownership than you've been trusted with before. YOU'LL FIT IF YOU - Are pursuing a degree in CS (or equivalent) and have built something real: a side project people actually used, open source contributions, a previous internship where you shipped. - Are comfortable in TypeScript, or good enough at programming that you'll be effective in it within a week. - Have played with LLMs beyond the chat box. Tool-calling, agent frameworks, React Flow, Yjs/CRDTs, or anything you hacked together at 2am are all table stakes. - Care about small details users never explicitly notice. - Are comfortable with uncertainty. We might implode tomorrow or we might grow 100,000,000% WoW next week. - Default to shipping. Let's get shit done. WHAT WE OFFER - $8500 monthly salary - $2500 monthly stipend for housing - $70 per diem for meals - In-person in NYC with a lean team of people who love the game, obsessed with building the future of creativity. If this is the kind of problem you're interested in, apply!

title: Hardware Engineer (FPGA/ASIC) Intern
qualification_text: Hardware Engineer (FPGA/ASIC) Internship, New York :: Jane Street New York, NY Jane Street is a quantitative trading firm and liquidity provider with a unique focus on technology and collaborative problem solving. Hardware Engineer (FPGA/ASIC) Internship, May-August LOCATION NYC DEPARTMENT Technology TEAM Software Engineering Apply Share this job About the Position Our goal is to give you a real sense of what it's like to work at Jane Street full time while also providing a truly unparalleled educational experience. As an intern, you are paired with full-time employees who act as mentors, collaborating with you on real-world projects we actually need done. In this internship, you'll learn how we use tools to make programming faster, more pleasant, and more reliable. We apply these same principles to our hardware engineering work, and we're looking for people who are interested in using programming language technology to improve the process of designing, testing, and validating hardware designs. We use Hardcaml, an OCaml library for succinctly describing hardware in RTL. Hardcaml is tightly integrated into our development environment, so you'll also gain lots of exposure to the libraries and tools that are foundational to our internal systems. No previous knowledge of Hardcaml is required. The hardware team at Jane Street works on both FPGA and ASIC designs. Depending on your background and experience, we'll craft a project that gives you exposure to our shared Hardcaml tech stack, as well as targeting an FPGA or ASIC platform. During the program, you'll dive deep on one project, mentored closely by the full-time employees who helped design it. Some intern projects consider big-picture questions that we're still trying to figure out, while others involve building something new. Your mentors will help you gain a better understanding of the wide range of problems we solve every day. We expect interns to build hardware applications from concept to a working design; your projects will predominantly involve OCaml & Hardcaml, for both RTL design and testing/integration. If you'd like to learn more, you can read about our interview process , meet some of our newest hires , or check out our OCaml All The Way Down talk and Programmable Hardware podcast episode. You can also learn more about Jane Street's internship program here . About You We don't expect you to have a background in finance, OCaml, functional programming, or any other specific field— we're looking for smart people who enjoy solving interesting problems. We're more interested in how you think and learn than what you currently know. You should be: Comfortable with a software programming language Experienced with a Hardware Description (or Construction) language (VHDL, Verilog, Chisel, Pymtl, or other), for both writing and testing hardware designs Experienced working with FPGA or ASIC vendor tools - Vivado or Quartus for FPGAs, Genus or Innovus for ASICs Experienced with building a working hardware project (either FPGA or ASIC) through an academic, professional, or personal project Interested in learning how to use FPGAs or ASICs in the context of networking If you're a recruiting agency and want to partner with us, please reach out to agency-partnerships@janestreet.com. Base salary is $300,000. title: Mechanical Engineer (Spring 2027 Co-op)
qualification_text: What We're Looking For We're looking for a Mechanical Engineering Co-op to join our team at FAB1, our first full-scale microfactory in Billerica, MA, this fall. This role is built for someone who loves the full loop of engineering: sketch it, model it, build it, test it, and fix it — fast. You'll rotate across active projects on our Mechanical Engineering team, working alongside engineers designing the workcells, fixturing, and production infrastructure that make our factory run. This is a hands-on role. You'll spend real time in the shop — cutting, welding, printing, and machining your own parts — not just handing drawings off to someone else. We move quickly here, so we need someone who can take a rough idea, iterate on it in CAD, get a physical version in hand, and improve it based on what they learn, on a tight timeline. What You'll Do - Design and Iterate Fast: Take on real mechanical design problems across FAB1 projects — fixtures, workstations, material handling, tooling — and move quickly from concept to CAD to working prototype. - Build What You Design: Fabricate and assemble your own prototypes and production hardware using mills, lathes, laser cutters, welders, 3D printers, and standard shop tools. - Rotate Across Projects: Work across multiple active workstreams on the ME team rather than a single fixed project, picking up context quickly and contributing wherever the team needs hands and ideas. - Test and Improve: Validate your designs on the shop floor, troubleshoot what doesn't work, and iterate toward a production-ready result. - Support Documentation: Produce clear CAD models and basic technical drawings that a teammate or vendor could build from. - Learn the Full Stack: Get exposure to how mechanical design connects to robotics, automation, and factory operations in a live manufacturing environment. Qualifications - Currently pursuing a BS in Mechanical Engineering or a related field; junior or senior standing preferred. - Solid CAD skills (Onshape, SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or similar) and the ability to go from a rough idea to a modeled part quickly. - Comfortable and safe operating shop tools and equipment — mills, lathes, laser cutters, welding, 3D printing, hand and power tools. - A fast learner who can pick up new tools, processes, and project context with minimal ramp-up. - Bias toward action: you'd rather build a rough prototype and learn from it than perfect a design on paper. - Strong communicator who works well within a team and can take direction from multiple engineers across rotating projects. - Available for a full-time, semester-length co-op in Billerica, MA this fall.
